relations.note: Kalku allegedly direct, bargain with, or exploit harmful forces against victims.
Some regional accounts describe witches dispatching this luminous nocturnal being.
A powerful witch may transform into, project, or travel as this flying head or night bird.

relations.myth: Spectral being exploited by harmful specialists
relations.note: Kalku are regionally associated with or said to exploit this dangerous nocturnal being.
Twentieth-century compilations sometimes classify this water creature as a wekufe usable by kalku.

relations.myth: Manipulation of a vulnerable dead spirit
relations.note: A kalku may allegedly capture or manipulate the spirit of a deceased person.

relations.myth: Missionary claims of dealings with the Devil
relations.note: Missionaries portrayed indigenous healers and alleged witches as dealing with or serving the Devil.
Chilote witches allegedly deform a stolen or surrendered infant into the cave-dwelling Invunche.

relations.myth: Invunche guards and advises the witches
relations.note: The Invunche allegedly guards the witches’ cave, advises them, and serves as an instrument of vengeance.
